sources.title: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production
First striking of half dollars from new coinage material

verifiedClaims.claim: The Kennedy half-dollar was authorized on December 30, 1963, following Kennedy’s November 22 assassination.
Proof dies were delivered January 2, 1964; Denver regular production began January 30; Philadelphia followed the next week; ceremonies took place February 11.
The initial half-dollar design used 90 percent silver, and the 1965 coinage transition reduced half-dollar silver content to 40 percent amid a silver shortage.

openQuestions: The Mint’s engraver recollection and Director Adams’s later letter describe different March dates for the first delivery/distribution; the transcript avoids that date.
missingEvidence: Catalog coin-0037 shows Kennedy half-dollar obverses, but its date is not established by the catalog. Inspect the full original and crop before use; do not identify it as a specific 1964 or 1965 issue.

stats.statement: Kennedy was assassinated November 22, 1963; the half-dollar act was approved December 30.
stats.source_name: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production

stats.statement: Proof dies arrived January 2, regular production began January 30 in Denver and the following week in Philadelphia, and ceremonies took place February 11.
stats.source_name: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production

stats.statement: The 1964 half-dollar was 90 percent silver; 1965 composition changed to 40 percent amid a silver shortage.
stats.source_name: First striking of half dollars from new coinage material

stats.statement: The Mint’s engravers recalled selecting the half dollar in late November 1963. The Franklin half had not completed its statutory 25-year design period, so Congress passed legislation authorizing the new design.
stats.source_name: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production

stats.statement: Gilroy Roberts designed the obverse and Frank Gasparro the reverse; the Mint recollection describes adapting existing models during the accelerated project.
stats.source_name: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production

stats.statement: Jacqueline Kennedy suggested portrait adjustments on December 17, 1963; the revised design received approval on December 27, before the December 30 act.
stats.source_name: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production

stats.statement: The Mint's recollection records an initial delivery of about 26 million Kennedy half dollars to the Federal Reserve on March 5, 1964.
stats.source_name: Mint engravers’ recollection of Kennedy half-dollar production
